vote.reason: Evidence checks out on the real files, independently re-derived. /home/user/ElmsNest/theme/sections/elmsnest-s-pdp-scene.liquid:83 sets `ens_op_lg = '50% 30%'` for solar-edison-string-lights, and lines 368/388 render the figure as `inline-size:100%` (sizes=100vw), `block-size:560px`, `object-fit:cover`, `object-position:var(--ens-op-lg)` at ≥ 901. The asset ens-pdp-edison.jpg is 1254×1254, so at 1366 the scale is 1.089, 514 source rows are visible, and 30% of the 740-row overflow puts the window at source rows 222–736 (my computation matches the reviewer's exactly). Measuring the source by column brightness at x 150/180/210: the first bulb's black socket/cap occupies rows ≈ 27–208 and the bright glass starts at row 208–238 and ends ≈ 640–654. The 30% window therefore starts 14+ rows below the socket's bottom edge: the socket is entirely outside the frame and the glass is cut at its neck — exactly what my own 1366×560 cover simulation (scratchpad/skeptic-edison-1366-30.png) shows, and it is pixel-identical to the reviewer's simulation (mean abs diff 0.24/255). The same holds at every desktop width (901: rows 142–922; 1920: 266–632 — the socket ends at ≈ 208), so no desktop viewport shows the socket at 30%; at 0% the window is rows 0–514 and the socket, cap and neck are whole with the base tip cut (the bulb is ≈ 620 rows tall, so it cannot be whole in a 514-row band). Scope: LEAD-DECISIONS.md row 9 is a 'Fixed in pass 2' ruling ('edison's first bulb beheaded at 1366 — Confirmed … `--ens-op-lg` 50% 30%'), and the amended SPEC §3 line 139 records the claimed outcome '(pass 2: the first bulb kept its socket at 1366)'; the critique D5 it answered complained specifically that 'the first, largest bulb has its socket outside the top edge'. That complaint is still literally true of the deployed value, and the SPEC statement is false — a fix that was recorded as landed but did not deliver what it says. No pass-2 render covers edison (verify-after has path/wall/flood/rope/deck only; verify-after-pass2.log and verify.json have no edison entry), so the ruling was never verified on a shot. Severity medium is fair: one product, desktop only, moved from mid-glass to neck. The proposed fix (`'50% 0%'`, correct the SPEC wording to say the tip is what the band gives up, add an edison shot to the verification) is concrete and consistent with the numbers.

finding.what: Ruling 10's guard ('no live pictured product → no photograph') fires only when the DEFAULT pictured product is also dead: when the owner has set `image_x` to his own frame and `pictured_x` to the product in it, and that product is later unpublished, `pictured_x` reads blank, the code substitutes the §3 default product, and the credit line names a product that is not the one in the owner's image — an uncredited/mis-credited sibling frame, the very state the ruling closed.

With `image_path != blank` (:213–214 → ens_kind 'picker') the credit at :344 prints `{{ ens_pictured.url }}` / `{{ ens_title_html }}` of the default product under the owner's image. Dormant path (scene_fallback default false, :429) — no mirrored page exercises it.
finding.fix: Tie the default pictured product to the default asset: substitute the §3 default only when the family's image picker is blank (`if ens_pictured == blank and section.settings.image_path == blank`); when the picker is set and the pictured product is blank, leave ens_pictured blank so the existing guard (:222) removes the photograph. Four one-line conditions, one per family.

vote.reason: Evidence checks out. (1) /home/user/ElmsNest/theme/sections/elmsnest-s-pdp-scene.liquid:180–183 (path), :189–192 (wall), :199–202 (spot), :208–211 (decor) read `assign ens_pictured = section.settings.pictured_x` and, `if ens_pictured == blank`, substitute `all_products['<§3 default>']`; :213–214 sets ens_kind 'picker' whenever `image_x` is set; the ruling-10 guard at :221–224 tests the already-substituted value, so it fires only when the §3 default is also not live. :290–292 sets `ens_title = ens_pictured.title` and :344 prints `{{ ens_pictured.url }}`/`{{ ens_title_html }}` — the credit therefore names the §3 default product under the owner's own picker image. (2) The premise holds: Shopify's settings doc (shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/architecture/settings) says a resource setting reads blank when 'the selected resource no longer exists, or the selected resource has been hidden' — a hidden/unpublished `pictured_x` is exactly the blank the code then overwrites with the default. (3) Scope: inside SPEC §2 item 4 (the owner option) and the amendment at the top of SPEC.md — 'the fallback option shows no photograph when its pictured product is not live' — which this state violates (the owner's pictured product is not live, a photograph shows, credited to a product not in it); LEAD-DECISIONS #10 ('no pictured product → no photograph') was implemented for E3's scenario (default handle dead) but not for this one. Mitigations that keep it low, as the reviewer rated it: the path is dormant (scene_fallback default false at :429; verify.json credit=false on every render), and it needs four owner actions (option on, own image, own pictured product, product later hidden). One caveat on the proposed fix: with a custom picker and pictured blank, SPEC §2.4's 'defaults = the products in §3' would no longer apply — acceptable since that credit would be equally unverifiable against an owner image, but the lead should note it as a §2.4 wording change.

vote.reason: The band is real but the finding's diagnosis, fix, and central claim are wrong, and it is out of scope. (1) Evidence checked: verify/scene-s.png, verify-wall/scene-s.png, verify-rope/scene-s.png are uniformly rgb(2,3,6) from row 550 down (measured), and the path/wall link box is y 542–568 (sizes.json), rope 567–593 — so yes, the ELEMENT shots at 360 cut the link. But the band is NOT the sticky add-to-cart bar: /home/user/ElmsNest/brief/side-pages/pdp2/shoot-sections.js already injects `.hdt-sticky-btn-atc,...,hdt-sticky-btn-atc{display:none!important}` before every element shot (the very rule the reviewer proposes to add from verify-mirror.js line 149), and a live reproduction on pdp2/verify-after/mirrors/pdp-path at 360×640 (scratchpad probe-r4.js, reproduces the identical 597-px shot with the band from row 550) shows at the moment of the shot: computed display of hdt-sticky-btn-atc = "none", elementsFromPoint(180,600) = a.ens-pdp-scene__link with no overlay above it, and the section sitting at viewport 66→662 (90→686 after Playwright's own scroll) — its bottom 46 px are below the 640 fold, and the capture paints that off-fold strip with the root ground (html/body background = rgb(2,3,6), the theme's --env2-sky-4). So the proposed fix is a no-op (rule already present) and the mechanism is wrong. (2) "The link at 360 has never been seen — only measured" is false: the harness's own 360 VIEWPORT shots show the link glyphs with no band — verify/scene-s-viewport.png rows 552–558 (40–48 bright px per row in the link's x range), verify-wall/scene-s-viewport.png rows 550–558, verify-rope/scene-s-viewport.png rows 576–582 (38–47 px per row, inside its 567–593 box); the viewport shot is pixel-identical to the element shot on rows 0–549 and the sticky bar is hidden there too. (3) Scope: SPEC §5 (line 203) requires section shots "at 390 and 1366 of A and B on path, wall, flood" — the 360 section shots are not an acceptance deliverable; LEAD-DECISIONS.md line 36 records that P5 binds at 390×844 and 360 is recorded for information; and the reviewer concedes "the page itself is fine". A cosmetic artefact of an extra harness output, with an incorrect cause and an already-applied fix, is not a page defect in SPEC §1–§5. Residual truth: if anyone wants the 360 element shots to include the section's last 46 px, the actual remedy is to shoot with the section's top at y=0 (as the -viewport step does) or a viewport ≥ section height — not hiding a bar that is already hidden.

(2) mtimes (ls --time-style=full-iso): log 22:47:38.707, verify.json 22:48:50.763; the log's own last line (37) says `wrote …/verify-after/verify.json`, yet the JSON on disk is 72 s newer — it was overwritten by a later run.
